title: Legacy Ultra vs X Subscription Ultra
topic: Legacy Ultra vs X Subscription Ultra
summary: New $200 X Subscription Ultra trades legacy Cursor Ultra's Claude/GPT allowance for a weekly shared Grok pool; switching is one-way.
synthesisHtml:
🌐 last30days v3.26.0 · synced 2026-10-16

What I learned:

Same price, different product. The X Subscription (launched 12 Oct 2026 by SpaceXSI/x.ai) bundles Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor and X Premium. Its Ultra tier is $200/month (Cursor's help page lists $2,000/yr annual) with "50x Plus" usage. Cursor staff confirmed on the forum that it "isn't the same as the previous Cursor Ultra plan", and legacy Ultra is closed to new signups.

The big loss is the third-party model allowance. Legacy Ultra dashboards show two monthly buckets, "Cursor Models" and "Other Models". On the new plans the fee covers only Grok model usage. Claude, GPT and other third-party models stay available in Cursor (Premium and above) but are billed separately at API list price through top-ups from the first request. x.ai says included third-party usage continues on current Cursor plans until you switch.

"2x usage" is about Grok coding usage, and nobody has defined it precisely yet. x.ai says each plan includes "at least twice as much coding usage with our models as the comparable Cursor plan". But the pool now refreshes weekly instead of monthly and is shared across Cursor, the Grok apps, the Grok tab on X and Grok Bot. Forum users (thread 174832, merged into the launch thread) are asking whether 2x means per week or per month, and whether Grok Bot usage can be billed at third-party API rates. There was no published absolute pool size at the time of the research. One switcher said their weekly pool drains like Grok Bot alone.

Switching is one-way, and the community reaction is split. You can keep your current plan or switch, with a prorated refund and limited-time offers. Legacy users treat switching as permanent, and long-time Ultra subscriber posts call the move a loss of Cursor's model neutrality. People who mostly code with Grok see the bundle as good value. Others want a purchasable plan that includes a third-party allowance and a commitment that legacy Ultra can be renewed indefinitely. YouTube explainers (13-15 Oct) mostly cover the cheaper Premium/Plus tiers.

Bottom line. If your daily driver is Claude or GPT in Cursor, stay on legacy Ultra while it lasts. If you mostly use Grok models and also want Grok Bot and X Premium, the new Ultra gives more Grok usage for the same $200. Wait for x.ai to publish the weekly pool size before you make the irreversible switch.
